record.title: Australia’s mandatory government AI policy adds a seven-pattern use classification
record.summary: Australia’s Digital Transformation Agency says version 2.1 of its mandatory Policy for the responsible use of AI in government was published on 21 October 2026. Its new Appendix D defines seven usage patterns and requires covered agencies to apply them in use-case registers, impact assessments and transparency statements. An independent comparison reports that this replaces a four-pattern classification and adds explicit categories for strategic support, workflow automation and coding while changing other definitions. The DTA describes the changes as minor; the exact v2.0 policy PDF was unavailable for direct comparison, and no agency implementation or outcome evidence is established.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The Digital Transformation Agency states that policy version 2.1 was published on 21 October 2026 as minor updates to version 2.0, which took effect on 15 December 2025.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Version 2.1 Appendix D defines seven AI-use patterns and requires agencies in scope to classify use in their internal use-case registers, when using the impact-assessment tool, and in public transparency statements.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: An independent document comparison reports that the v2.0 classification had four patterns, while v2.1 adds strategic support, workflow automation and coding, narrows workplace productivity, and redefines decision-making around effects on rights or interests. The exact v2.0 policy PDF was not directly available in this review.

evidence_gaps.description: The official v2.0 policy PDF used for the reported comparison was not accessible from the DTA link during this review; the current media endpoint returns v2.1 and the old document path returns 404. The precise taxonomy delta is supported by a detailed secondary comparison but not independently checked against the predecessor bytes.
The policy text establishes classification requirements but the extent and timing of agency updates to registers, assessments and public statements were not measured.

brief.importance_rationale: A classification required across Commonwealth AI registers, impact assessments and public transparency statements can change how public-sector AI use is described and compared. This could affect oversight and interpretation across agencies if the new categories are adopted consistently; it does not establish new binding controls, implementation or outcomes.
limitations: The DTA calls the 21 October changes minor; the detailed v2.0-to-v2.1 comparison in this record comes from a secondary source whose saved predecessor PDF was not independently retrieved.
No evidence establishes that agencies have updated their registers, assessment workflows or transparency statements to the new classification.
The policy classification change does not itself prove new controls, improved oversight or measured public-sector AI outcomes.
brief.summary: Australia’s Digital Transformation Agency says version 2.1 of its mandatory Policy for the responsible use of AI in government was published on 21 October 2026. Its new Appendix D defines seven usage patterns and requires covered agencies to apply them in use-case registers, impact assessments and transparency statements. An independent comparison reports that this replaces a four-pattern classification and adds explicit categories for strategic support, workflow automation and coding while changing other definitions. The DTA describes the changes as minor; the exact v2.0 policy PDF was unavailable for direct comparison, and no agency implementation or outcome evidence is established.

technical.claimed_result: A secondary document comparison of saved v2.0 and v2.1 PDFs reports three added usage patterns and changes to existing definitions. The exact v2.0 file was not retrieved or independently diffed in this activation.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official v2.1 page dates its publication and labels its updates minor; Appendix D directly states the seven categories and three mandatory classification surfaces.
technical.implementation_status: Policy version 2.1 published; agency adoption of new labels, updated forms and effects on registers or transparency statements were not measured.
technical.mechanism: The policy assigns each in-scope AI use case a usage-pattern and domain classification for shared reporting in agency registers, impact assessment and transparency statements. Appendix D provides seven usage patterns.
technical.regime: Mandatory policy for non-corporate Commonwealth entities, with stated exceptions; corporate Commonwealth entities are encouraged to apply it.
technical.reproducibility: Official v2.1 policy page and Appendix D are directly inspectable. The exact v2.0 comparison was not reproduced because the official prior PDF endpoint currently serves v2.1 or returns 404.
technical.strongest_baseline: The accessible DTA v1.1 transparency standard’s Attachment A lists four patterns; the exact v2.0 policy PDF was unavailable. A secondary comparison reports the v2.0-to-v2.1 change.

brief.title: Australia’s mandatory government AI policy adds a seven-pattern use classification
brief.why_it_matters: A shared classification used in government registers, impact assessments and public statements shapes how agencies describe and compare their AI use. If the reported taxonomy changes are adopted consistently, separate categories for coding, workflow automation and strategic support could make government AI inventories easier to interpret. The version update does not itself demonstrate new risk controls or implementation outcomes.
